title: Hyderabad, September 1948
note: Hand-checked cards for the end of Hyderabad State (Operation Polo, 13-18 September 1948). Villagers only say these lines; no source names are shown in the game. Step 18b: lines with today/yesterday hold for their own day ("to"); 15 September and the days after 18 September have their own lines.

refer.text: That is court business. I wouldn't know. Ask the clerks at [[king_kothi|King Kothi Palace]].

news.text: Have you heard? Hyderabad has told the [[un|United Nations]] that India may invade.
The Indian Army entered the state at four this morning. India calls it a [[polo|police action]].
Have you heard? The Indian Army has entered the state. India calls it a [[polo|police action]]. They fought at [[naldurg|Naldurg]] yesterday.
The fighting goes on. They say the army has taken [[suryapet|Suryapet]] in the east.
The army is near [[zahirabad|Zahirabad]], and the [[un|UN Security Council]] takes up Hyderabad's complaint today, in Paris.
The Hyderabad army has surrendered at [[secunderabad|Secunderabad]].
Everyone at court is waiting for news from the [[un|United Nations]].
The Indian Army crossed into the state this morning. India calls it a [[polo|police action]].
The army is fighting in the west and in the east. [[aurangabad|Aurangabad]] has surrendered.
In the east the army has taken [[suryapet|Suryapet]]; in the west it has reached Latur.
The [[un|Security Council]] takes up our complaint in Paris today.
A heavy day. This morning the prime minister, [[laiq_ali|Mir Laiq Ali]], and the whole cabinet resigned.
It is over. [[el_edroos|General El Edroos]] has surrendered to [[chaudhuri|General Chaudhuri]].

answers.text: India's army has marched into [[hyderabad_state|Hyderabad State]] to make it join India. [[nizam|The Nizam]] wants to stay independent. India calls it a 'police action'.
The army came in at dawn on the Solapur road. They are fighting at [[naldurg|Naldurg fort]], {d:naldurg}. Another army came from the east, to [[kodad|Kodad]].
Yesterday they fought at [[naldurg|Naldurg fort]], {d:naldurg}. Today the eastern army is fighting near [[suryapet|Suryapet]], {d:suryapet}, and [[aurangabad|Aurangabad]] has surrendered.
In the west the army has reached Latur. In the east it has taken [[suryapet|Suryapet]], {d:suryapet}.
The army is on the Solapur road near [[zahirabad|Zahirabad]], {d:zahirabad}.
This morning the army entered [[bidar|Bidar]]. Another column is at [[chityal|Chityal]], about 60 km from the city. At five this evening [[nizam|the Nizam]] announced a ceasefire.
It is over. This afternoon an Indian armoured column came into the city, and the Hyderabad army surrendered at [[secunderabad|Secunderabad]], {d:secunderabad}.
It is over. On 18 September an Indian armoured column came into the city, and the Hyderabad army surrendered at [[secunderabad|Secunderabad]], {d:secunderabad}.
This morning, at four o'clock.
Yesterday, 13 September, at four in the morning.
On 13 September, two days ago.
On 13 September, three days ago.
On 13 September. This evening at five, the Nizam announced a ceasefire.
On 13 September. The fighting stopped with the ceasefire yesterday evening.
It began on 13 September, and the fighting stopped with the ceasefire on the evening of 17 September.
The Indian Army, led by [[chaudhuri|Major General J. N. Chaudhuri]], against the Nizam's army and the [[razakars|Razakars]].
The Indian Army, led by [[chaudhuri|Major General J. N. Chaudhuri]], against the Nizam's army and the [[razakars|Razakars]]. Now there is a ceasefire.
The Indian Army, led by [[chaudhuri|Major General J. N. Chaudhuri]], against the Nizam's army and the [[razakars|Razakars]]. The Hyderabad army has surrendered.
About 35,000 Indian troops. The state's own army has about 22,000 men, and the [[razakars|Razakars]] are said to number about 200,000.

later.text: 17 September, 5 pm: the Nizam announces a ceasefire.
18 September, about 4 pm: General Chaudhuri's armoured column enters Hyderabad. Major General El Edroos surrenders the Hyderabad army at Secunderabad.
Hyderabad becomes part of India, as Hyderabad State (1948–1956).
Violence during and after the operation: an official committee led by Pandit Sunder Lal gave a 'very conservative estimate' of 27,000–40,000 deaths. Other scholars put it at 200,000 or more.

cards.title: The Nizam: Mir Osman Ali Khan

answers.text: Mir Osman Ali Khan, the seventh Nizam, Asaf Jah VII. He has ruled [[hyderabad_state|Hyderabad State]] since 1911.
Mir Osman Ali Khan, the seventh Nizam. He has ruled since 1911. This evening he announced a ceasefire.
Mir Osman Ali Khan, the seventh Nizam, ruler since 1911. Yesterday he announced the ceasefire.
Mir Osman Ali Khan, the seventh Nizam, ruler since 1911. On 17 September he announced the ceasefire.
At [[king_kothi|King Kothi Palace]], {d:king_kothi}. He never moved to [[chowmahalla|Chowmahalla Palace]], where his father lived.
He was born in Hyderabad in 1886, so he is 62 this year.
His father was [[mahbub|Mahbub Ali Khan]], the sixth Nizam. His sons are [[azam_jah|Azam Jah]] and [[moazzam_jah|Moazzam Jah]]. The family is the [[asaf_jahi|Asaf Jahi dynasty]].
His prime minister is [[laiq_ali|Mir Laiq Ali]], since late 1947. Before him it was the [[chhatari|Nawab of Chhatari]].
This morning [[laiq_ali|Mir Laiq Ali]] and the whole cabinet resigned. The Nizam asked for it last night.
[[laiq_ali|Mir Laiq Ali]] and the whole cabinet resigned yesterday morning.
[[laiq_ali|Mir Laiq Ali]] and the whole cabinet resigned on the morning of 17 September.

later.text: 1950–1956: Rajpramukh, the head of Hyderabad State inside India.
Dies on 24 February 1967 at King Kothi and is buried at the Judi Mosque, facing his home.

answers.text: [[nizam|The Nizam]]'s palace, also called Nazri Bagh. The eastern half is used for official work and ceremonies; the western half is his home.
It is {d:king_kothi}.
A noble, Kamal Khan, built it. [[mahbub|The Nizam's father]] bought it, and the Nizam moved in when he was 13. He stayed on after he became Nizam in 1911.
Kamal Khan put his initials, KK, on everything, even the doors and window grilles. So the palace was called King Kothi, the 'King's house'.
Look at the curtain on the main gate, the purdah. When the Nizam goes out, it is lifted; while it is down, he is at home.

later.text: The Nizam lives here until his death in 1967.
One of its buildings, Usman Mansion, is pulled down in the early 1980s; a hospital stands in its place.

answers.text: The Nizam's prime minister since late 1947.
He was the Nizam's prime minister from late 1947. This morning he and the whole cabinet resigned.
He was the prime minister until he and the whole cabinet resigned yesterday morning.
He was the Nizam's prime minister from late 1947 until he and the whole cabinet resigned on 17 September.
Muhammad Ahmad Said Khan, the Nawab of Chhatari. He was the Nizam's prime minister until November 1947.

later.text: 23 September 1948: in a radio speech the Nizam says that a group led by Qasim Razvi forced Chhatari and other trusted ministers to resign in November 1947.

answers.text: Armed volunteers who back the Nizam's government and fight against joining India. Their leader is [[razvi|Qasim Razvi]].
Nobody knows exactly. Some say about 200,000.

later.text: Their leader, Qasim Razvi, surrenders after the operation.

answers.text: The leader of the [[razakars|Razakars]]. He was born in 1902.

later.text: He surrenders after the operation, and dies in 1970.

answers.text: He leads the Indian Army's attack on [[hyderabad_state|Hyderabad State]].
He led the Indian Army's attack. This afternoon the Hyderabad army surrendered to him.
He led the Indian Army's attack. On 18 September the Hyderabad army surrendered to him.

later.text: 18 September: the Hyderabad army surrenders to him at Secunderabad.
He later becomes Chief of the Indian Army.

answers.text: Syed Ahmed El Edroos, commander of the Hyderabad State Army.
Syed Ahmed El Edroos, commander of the Hyderabad State Army. After the ceasefire the Nizam sent him orders to keep the people safe.
Syed Ahmed El Edroos, commander of the Hyderabad State Army. This afternoon he surrendered to [[chaudhuri|General Chaudhuri]] at Secunderabad.
Syed Ahmed El Edroos, commander of the Hyderabad State Army. On 18 September he surrendered to [[chaudhuri|General Chaudhuri]] at Secunderabad.

later.text: 18 September: he surrenders the Hyderabad State Forces to General Chaudhuri at Secunderabad.

answers.text: India's prime minister.
India's prime minister. Today he spoke on the radio about the end of the fighting.
India's prime minister. On 18 September he spoke on the radio about the end of the fighting.

later.text: 18 September: in a radio broadcast he says it is natural to rejoice at the 'swift termination' of the action.

answers.text: India's deputy prime minister and home minister, one of the leaders behind the action against Hyderabad.
India's Agent General in Hyderabad, India's man in our city.
India's Agent General in Hyderabad. This afternoon the Nizam called him to his office.
India's Agent General in Hyderabad. On 17 September the Nizam called him to his office.

later.text: 17 September, 4 pm: the Nizam tells him, “The vultures have resigned. I don't know what to do.” Munshi advises him to order the army commander to keep the people safe.

answers.text: On 21 August Hyderabad asked the UN Security Council to look at its dispute with India.
On 21 August Hyderabad took its dispute with India to the UN Security Council. Now it has told the Council of a threat of invasion.
Hyderabad has told the UN Security Council that India has invaded.
Today the Security Council, meeting in Paris, put Hyderabad's complaint on its agenda.
The Security Council took up Hyderabad's complaint yesterday, in Paris.
On 16 September the Security Council, meeting in Paris, put Hyderabad's complaint on its agenda.
At the UN Security Council. This month it is meeting in Paris.

later.text: 20–24 September: the complaint is withdrawn; the Nizam's cable of 22 September confirms it.

answers.text: A princely state ruled by [[nizam|the Nizam]]. Its capital is Hyderabad. When the British left India in August 1947, the Nizam chose to stay independent.
[[nizam|The Nizam]], Mir Osman Ali Khan.
[[nizam|The Nizam]] is still the Nizam, but the Indian Army now holds the state.

later.text: After the operation it becomes part of India, as Hyderabad State (1948–1956).

answers.text: The family of the Nizams. They have ruled Hyderabad since 1724, when Asaf Jah I made it his own. [[nizam|The Nizam]] is the seventh Asaf Jah.

later.text: 1967: his grandson Mukarram Jah is given the title Asaf Jah VIII.

cards.title: Mahbub Ali Khan, Asaf Jah VI

answers.text: The sixth Nizam, who ruled from 1869 to 1911, and the Nizam's father. He bought [[king_kothi|King Kothi]] and lived at [[chowmahalla|Chowmahalla Palace]].
The Nizam's elder son, the Prince of Berar.

later.text: 1967: his son Mukarram Jah becomes Asaf Jah VIII.

answers.text: The Nizam's younger son.
The palace where the Nizam's father, [[mahbub|Mahbub Ali Khan]], lived. The Nizam chose to stay at [[king_kothi|King Kothi]] instead.
It is {d:chowmahalla}.
The great monument with four minarets at the heart of the old city. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built it in 1591.
It is {d:charminar}.
A fort on the Solapur–Secunderabad road. The first battle of the operation was fought here on 13 September.
It is {d:naldurg}.

A town on the road from the east. The Indian Army took it today.
A town on the road from the east. The Indian Army took it on 15 September.

later.text: 15 September: the Indian Army occupies Suryapet.

answers.text: A town on the Solapur–Hyderabad road. The army is passing it today.
A town on the Solapur–Hyderabad road. The army passed it on 16 September.
It is {d:zahirabad}.
The Indian Army entered Bidar early this morning.
The Indian Army entered Bidar early on 17 September.
It is {d:bidar}.
A city in the north of the state. It surrendered to the Indian Army today.
A city in the north of the state. It surrendered to the Indian Army on 14 September.
It is {d:aurangabad}.
A town on the road from the east. The eastern army reached it this morning.
A town on the road from the east. The eastern army reached it on the morning of 13 September.
It is {d:kodad}.
A town on the eastern road, about 60 km from the city. An Indian armoured column is here today.
A town on the eastern road, about 60 km from the city. An armoured column was here on 17 September.
The twin city just north of Hyderabad.
The twin city just north of Hyderabad. The Hyderabad army surrendered here this afternoon.
The twin city just north of Hyderabad. The Hyderabad army surrendered here on 18 September.

stories.headline: Hyderabad tells the UN of a threat of invasion
stories.text: Hyderabad, which took its dispute with India to the [[un|UN Security Council]] on 21 August, has now told the Council of a threat of invasion.

stories.headline: Indian Army enters the state
stories.text: Indian forces crossed into [[hyderabad_state|Hyderabad State]] at four this morning. India calls it a [[polo|police action]].

stories.headline: Fighting at Naldurg fort
stories.text: The first battle was fought at [[naldurg|Naldurg fort]], on the Solapur road.

stories.headline: Eastern column at Kodad
stories.text: Another column came from the east and reached [[kodad|Kodad]] this morning.

stories.headline: Aurangabad surrenders
stories.text: In the north, [[aurangabad|Aurangabad]] surrendered to the Indian Army this afternoon.

stories.headline: Fighting near Suryapet
stories.text: The eastern column of the [[polo|police action]] is fighting near [[suryapet|Suryapet]].

stories.headline: Street fighting in Osmanabad
stories.text: Osmanabad was taken after heavy street fighting with the [[razakars|Razakars]].

stories.headline: Army nears Zahirabad
stories.text: The Indian column on the Solapur road has reached [[zahirabad|Zahirabad]].

stories.headline: Latur and Suryapet taken
stories.text: Yesterday the Indian Army took Latur and [[suryapet|Suryapet]].

stories.headline: Hyderabad's case at the UN
stories.text: The [[un|Security Council]], meeting in Paris, put Hyderabad's complaint on its agenda today.

stories.headline: Nizam announces ceasefire
stories.text: At five this evening [[nizam|the Nizam]] announced a ceasefire.

stories.headline: Prime minister and cabinet resign
stories.text: [[laiq_ali|Mir Laiq Ali]] and the whole cabinet resigned this morning.

stories.headline: Army in Bidar; a column at Chityal
stories.text: The Indian Army entered [[bidar|Bidar]] early today. An armoured column is at [[chityal|Chityal]], about 60 km from the city.

stories.headline: Hyderabad army surrenders
stories.text: At about four this afternoon an Indian armoured column entered the city. [[el_edroos|Major General El Edroos]] surrendered the Hyderabad army to [[chaudhuri|Major General J. N. Chaudhuri]] at [[secunderabad|Secunderabad]].

stories.headline: Nehru speaks on the radio
stories.text: [[nehru|Jawaharlal Nehru]] said in a broadcast that it was natural to rejoice at the 'swift termination' of the action.
